baselineCommitMessage: ops(vercel): remove completed one-time domain cutover workflow

evidence.finding: Next 16.2.10, React 19.2.7, Payload, Directus, Supabase and Resend are installed; Convex, Clerk, Stripe and Workflow are absent; goal and Graphify scripts are not exposed.
Documents the current Supabase/Payload-era target and commands that do not match package.json.
Documents Supabase, Directus, Resend, Cal.com and Agent OS variables but omits the approved target integrations.
Requires Graphify-first discovery and goal verification while retaining stale global design constraints.
Explicitly rejects a full Convex migration and therefore conflicts with the approved architecture.
Generated specialists still route API and frontend work toward Supabase and the old design rules.
Only enables hooks; no economy, concurrency, verbosity, or Graphify defaults are defined.
Graphify is bound to one absolute Windows path.
Implements the complete RPI goal loop, but package.json does not expose it.
Implements budgeted Graphify query/path/explain/update commands, but package.json does not expose them.
Defines /goal as research-plan-implement with deterministic verification.
Wraps the app with Payload and permits public Supabase storage and Directus assets.
Contains current security headers, redirects, SEO cron, and legacy provider host allowances.
Protects the Supabase portal but does not protect /manage.
Persistence errors are logged and swallowed before the route returns success; provider effects execute inline.
Requires market, timeline, and contactMethod and uses a process-local Map rate limiter.
Stores complete unsent leads in localStorage and receives permanent public photo URLs.
Submits an incomplete lead payload without required market, timeline, and contactMethod fields.
Sets noindex metadata but is not an authorization boundary.
Client-side Supabase admin permits sign-up and browser CRUD against business/content tables.
Returns a signed upload URL plus a permanent public lead-photo URL.
Only ratings four and five receive the Google-review path.
Places the referrer's email in the referral URL and analytics payload.
Returns notFound for slugs absent from the static service-page registry.
Acts as a static service/location route registry that can drift from navigation, redirects, and sitemap.
Uses Directus, then Supabase, then static fallbacks, creating three publication sources.
Directus remains an active content adapter.
Payload uses Supabase Postgres and S3 and includes an unsafe known-secret fallback.
Associates portal resources to authenticated users by matching email strings.
Only emits browser events and cannot reconcile events to canonical revenue facts.
Executes delivery effects without first creating a canonical durable lead.
Several tests explicitly require unsafe legacy behavior, including review gating and PII browser persistence.
Provides a useful but stale Supabase/Payload architecture map.
